title: Free-variable consumption invariant of the Razborov encoder
statement: Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n$ Boolean variables in which, within each term, any two literals on the same variable are equal and no literal occurs more than once, and fix an arbitrary width $w \in \bbn$. Let $\rho_0$ and $\sigma$ be restrictions on these $n$ variables that leave exactly the same variables free (for every variable $v$, $\rho_0(v)$ is unset iff $\sigma(v)$ is), and let $\mathrm{path}$ be a prefix of the deepest root-to-leaf path of the canonical decision tree for $f|_{\rho_0}$, of length at most the depth of that tree. If the fuel parameter strictly exceeds the length of $\mathrm{path}$, then the restriction returned by the Razborov encoder run on $f$ with width $w$, this fuel, $\mathrm{path}$, $\rho_0$, and $\sigma$ has exactly $\lvert\mathrm{path}\rvert$ fewer free variables than $\sigma$; that is, its number of free variables plus $\lvert\mathrm{path}\rvert$ equals the number of free variables of $\sigma$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a DNF formula on n Boolean variables
within each term, two literals sharing a variable are equal
each term has no duplicate literals
fuel strictly exceeds the path length
rho_0 and sigma leave exactly the same variables free
path is a prefix of the canonical tree's deepest path for f under rho_0
path length at most the canonical tree depth
replaced:
When the canonical tree depth is at least the path length,
$\mathrm{razborovEncode.go}$ fully consumes the path (never terminating early),
and the resulting $\sigma$ has $\mathrm{numFree}$ decreased by exactly the initial
path length: $(\mathrm{go}\,\dots).1.\mathrm{numFree} + \mathrm{path.length} = \sigma.\mathrm{numFree}$.
